patterns.name: Adjacent cross-region continuation
patterns.observable_criteria: A verified direct TAB transition between clearly distinct page regions, such as header to main, main to footer, or adjacent visual panels. The destination must have inferred meaningful position exactly one greater than the source. The page-region boundary must be independently supported by screenshot, DOM, or KFG evidence. Exclude backward, cyclic, and wraparound edges, as well as transitions within a single form, panel, or component.

patterns.name: Cyclic or wraparound focus edge
patterns.observable_criteria: A TAB transition from a later or end-of-page control back to an earlier control, often near the top or beginning of the page.

patterns.name: Local auxiliary-control progression
patterns.observable_criteria: A transition between nearby secondary utility, support, or auxiliary controls within the same local functional group. Both endpoints must serve genuinely secondary functions, such as help, settings, recovery, or support. A logo, ordinary promotional call to action, primary form input, or primary submit action does not qualify solely because it is nearby or represented by a link. If endpoint roles are unclear, classify UNCERTAIN.

patterns.name: Browser-to-page entry
patterns.observable_criteria: A modeled transition from the virtual Browser boundary to the documented first focused webpage control.

patterns.name: Consecutive cross-subgroup transition
patterns.observable_criteria: A verified direct TAB transition between clearly distinct visual or functional subgroups, with destination inferred meaningful position exactly one greater than the source. Both subgroup distinction and adjacency are required. Ordinary moves between fields or buttons in one form do not qualify. Direct KFG connectivity alone does not establish meaningful-order consecutiveness.

patterns.name: Field-to-field transition near embedded helper link
patterns.observable_criteria: A direct TAB transition between primary form fields where a separate focusable helper or recovery link is visually or structurally associated with the destination field group.

patterns.name: Auxiliary-link transition across workflow controls
patterns.observable_criteria: A direct TAB transition originating from a helper, recovery, or support link, with one or more primary workflow controls located between its endpoints in the inferred meaningful or visual order.

patterns.name: Primary-control transition over local controls
patterns.observable_criteria: A direct TAB transition from a primary control to a later control in the same functional module, where at least one separate visible focusable control occupies an intermediate meaningful or visual position. Identify the intermediate control using the navigation JSON, screenshot, or KFG. The intermediate control need not be permanently unreachable: this pattern concerns bypassing it in the specific direct transition. Do not infer a skipped control from a numeric position gap alone.

patterns.name: Backward local focus transition
patterns.observable_criteria: A direct TAB transition moving backward in inferred meaningful order within the same localized form row, interactive component, or content cluster. Page-wide wraparound transitions and movements between separate page regions do not qualify.
